ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Jane Austen — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Austen is a 40-year-old novelist with primary adrenal insufficiency diagnosed four months ago, on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone, who comes for her yearly preventive visit. She finished the draft of the novel she was writing earlier this month and says she has not had such a run of good mornings for a year. She walks to the market town and back most days. She has had no illness needing stress doses since the sore throat in the spring, and she carries her injection kit and wears her medical ID. Her periods are regular. She has no new concerns. [S]

tr.td: Well on hydrocortisone 10 mg and 5 mg and fludrocortisone 0.1 mg; no crisis

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation; its timing echoes the documented break in her health (D).

Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease): no cortisol response to cosyntropin with a markedly raised ACTH, and mineralocorticoid deficiency with raised renin and low aldosterone; on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone; synthetic modern diagnosis chosen for a historical illness whose cause is disputed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the historical cause of her illness remains undetermined (R, disputed).

Guideline basis: Diagnosis and Treatment of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline (2016); Medicare Preventive Services reference: visit templates, screening cascades, and documentation elements (2026); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026)

Follow-up: Six-month review in the autumn with electrolytes, renin, TSH, the PHQ-9, the second hepatitis B dose and the influenza vaccine. HIV, hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HPV results by phone. Mammogram as booked. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1816-10-12: seven-month review: replacement, renin, thyroid, mood, and the closing of the differential. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She wants full treatment in any emergency, and wants emergency staff to give hydrocortisone at once if she is found unwell; a copy of her emergency letter is in the chart and in her purse. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and chose not to record other treatment preferences today. To be revisited yearly. [S]
